name: ASAP3
description: 3rd-gen ASAP sensor with large fluorescence modulation and fast kinetics.

spectrum.name: ASAP3
spectrum.note: No one-photon excitation/emission spectrum is published for ASAP3: the Villette 2019 paper reports only imaging filter settings (ex 490/10, em 525/40 — a collection band, not a peak) and no spectral figure, and FPbase has no ASAP entry. ASAP3 shares the cpsfGFP-OPT (superfolder GFP) chromophore of ASAP1/ASAP2s (derived from ASAP2f via L146G/S147T/S150G/H151D/R414Q; EGFP was used only as a brightness control) and is not spectrally red-shifted, so the FPbase Superfolder GFP excitation/emission curve is used as a fluorophore proxy. Replaces a fabricated curve that was the FPbase EGFP spectrum red-shifted +16 nm (ex) / +14 nm (em) to fake peaks of 505/525. Re-verified 2026-09 against the live FPbase API (/api/proteins/spectra/?name__iexact=Superfolder GFP): the stored arrays are byte-identical to FPbase's Superfolder GFP default_ex (188 pts, 352-539 nm) and default_em (160 pts, 469-628 nm), max abs difference 0.000000. peakEm corrected 511 -> 509 nm to match the stored curve's own argmax (peakEx 490 nm already did); FPbase's tabulated summary values for this protein are 488/510 nm, which are rounded reads of the same curve.

voltage.name: ASAP3
voltage.note: Derived curve: the steady-state response SHAPE was digitized from the green ASAP3 Boltzmann in Fig. 2A (normalized (F−Fmin)/(Fmax−Fmin)), then converted to ΔF/F relative to −70 mV by solving the absolute floor Fmin/Fmax ≈ 0.24 from the Table 1 anchor (ΔF/F per 100-mV step −70→+30 mV = −51%). Re-digitized 2026-07-07 (color-mask + Boltzmann fit, V½ ≈ −85 mV, k ≈ 31; max residual 1.3% vs the prior digitization — confirmed faithful to Fig. 2A) and resampled onto an even 20-mV grid (−110→+30 mV, anchored at −70 = 0). The depolarizing side is well constrained; the hyperpolarizing side is steeper than the directly-measured subthreshold slope (0.46%/mV, Fig. S5E) because the Fig. 2A Boltzmann is full steady-state whereas the subthreshold measurement is kinetically attenuated.

Amplitude-weighted mean of the bi-exponential fit at 37°C in HEK293A cells imaged at 1888 fps under simultaneous voltage clamp (ASAP5 paper, Table S2; ASAP3 row, 37°C). Activation (−70→+30 mV depolarization): τ_fast=1.3 ms (73%), τ_slow=45.5 ms (27%) → weighted on=13.23 ms. Deactivation (repolarization): τ_fast=3.5 ms (81%), τ_slow=3.9 ms (19%) → weighted off=3.58 ms. Corrected from a prior entry that stored the fast components only (1.3/3.5) and mislabeled the temperature as 25°C — those values are the 37°C τ-fast pair, not a room-temperature measurement. The same table also lists a 23°C ASAP3 row (act τ_fast 3.6/63%, τ_slow 18.5; deact τ_fast 9.0/29%, τ_slow 22.8 → weighted 9.11/18.80).

Amplitude-weighted mean of the bi-exponential fit at 22-23°C in HEK293 cells (Table 1; Table S1, -70→+30 mV step). Activation: τ_fast=3.7 ms (81%), τ_slow=48 ms → weighted on=12.12 ms. Deactivation: τ_fast=16.0 ms (81%), τ_slow=102 ms → weighted off=32.34 ms.

Amplitude-weighted mean of the bi-exponential fit at 32-35°C in HEK293A cells under whole-cell voltage clamp, −70→+30 mV (JEDI-2P paper, Table S2; ASAP3 column, n=16 cells). Activation: τ_fast=0.98 ms (82.4%), τ_slow=20.9 ms → weighted on=4.49 ms. Deactivation: τ_fast=4.29 ms (86.9%), τ_slow=136 ms → weighted off=21.54 ms. Previously stored the fast components only (0.98/4.29). Cell line corrected from 'HEK293-Kir2.1' — the Table S2 legend specifies HEK293A cells (HEK293-Kir2.1 was used for the photostability/brightness panels in that paper, not for kinetics).

Amplitude-weighted mean of the bi-exponential fit at 21-23°C in HEK293A cells under whole-cell voltage clamp, −70→+30 mV (JEDI-2P paper, Table S2; ASAP3 column, n=9 cells). Activation: τ_fast=2.26 ms (78.4%), τ_slow=32.2 ms → weighted on=8.73 ms. Deactivation: τ_fast=11.0 ms (85.3%), τ_slow=112 ms → weighted off=25.85 ms. Previously stored the fast components only (2.26/11). Cell line corrected from 'HEK293-Kir2.1' — the Table S2 legend specifies HEK293A cells.

Amplitude-weighted mean of the bi-exponential fit at 23°C in HEK293A cells imaged at 1888 fps under simultaneous voltage clamp (ASAP5 paper, Table S2; ASAP3 row, 23°C, n=6-9 cells). Activation (−70→+30 mV): τ_fast=3.6 ms (63%), τ_slow=18.5 ms (37%) → weighted on=9.11 ms. Deactivation (+30→−70 mV): τ_fast=9.0 ms (29%), τ_slow=22.8 ms (71%) → weighted off=18.80 ms. Companion room-temperature row to the 37°C entry from the same table; previously only described in that entry's note and not stored.

Steady-state response to a 100-mV voltage step (−70 → +30 mV) under one-photon widefield 470/24-nm illumination in HEK293A cells at room temperature, measured alongside JEDI-1P (≈55%) and ASAP2s (≈29%); n = 7 cells. Value read off the Fig. 2c mean line (y-axis '−%ΔF/F0'); the matching Fig. 2b F-V curve gives the same amplitude at +30 mV. Cross-GEVI entry from the JEDI-1P origin paper (primary subject JEDI-1P).

sensitivityData.note: ΔF/F per single AP (17.9 ± 1.2%) in cultured hippocampal neurons under one-photon widefield illumination at room temperature (Table 1, Voltage Responsivity 1-Photon; Fig. 2E/2F).

ASAP3-Kv optical spike amplitude (10.2% ΔF/F, with an empirical SNR of 2.8) under one-photon widefield 453-nm illumination at 100 mW/mm², recorded IN VIVO from mouse hippocampal SST+ interneurons at 1,000 fps (Evans et al. 2023, main text: 'optical AP amplitudes averaged 10.2% for ASAP3-Kv and 11.5% for ASAP4e-Kv ... (Fig. 3c)'). Prep corrected 2026-09 from a prior note that said 'cultured neurons' — Figs. 2 and 3 of that paper are in vivo hippocampal SST+ interneuron recordings.

ASAP3-Kv peak fluorescence response to current-evoked single APs in dissociated rat hippocampal neurons (DIV14-16) at 32-35°C under one-photon widefield 470/24-nm illumination; n = 5 neurons, mean ≈ 16.5 −%ΔF/F0 read off the Fig. 2n mean line (JEDI-1P-Kv ≈ 26.5% in the same panel). Cross-GEVI entry from the JEDI-1P origin paper.

ASAP3-Kv ΔF/F per action potential in mouse cortex layer 2/3 brain slices, imaged on a confocal microscope with 488-nm excitation / 525-50-nm emission at ~500 Hz; APs evoked via CoChR. Computed from the paper's own Ext. Data Fig. 5c source data (MOESM12 spreadsheet, 'Extended Data Figure 5c' sheet): n = 18 neurons, mean 10.24% (median 9.10%, range 3.3-18.9%). Cross-GEVI entry from the SomArchon paper (primary subject SomArchon, mean 53.5% in the same panel).
ΔF/F per single AP (17.0 ± 0.8%) in cultured hippocampal slices at 32°C under random-access multiphoton (two-photon) excitation, significantly larger than ASAP2s (11.7 ± 0.7%).
ΔF/F per single AP (8.3 ± 1.1%) in cerebellar molecular layer interneurons (very narrow spikes, FWHM 0.43 ms) at 34°C under two-photon RAMP microscopy, outperforming ASAP2s (5.3 ± 0.9%).

ASAP3-Kv reported single current-evoked APs with ΔF/F of 37.3 ± 4.1% (mean ± SD, n = 8 spikes) at 22°C in acute mouse striatal slices, under two-photon line scanning at 1 kHz along the soma with a signal-to-noise ratio of 2.6 ± 0.39 (Villette et al. 2019, Figs. 3H and S6D). Substantially larger than the 17% recorded in cultured hippocampal slices (Fig. 3C) — the Kv2.1-targeted soma-restricted construct concentrates the signal. Small sample (spikes from a single prep), so treat as an upper-end 2P value.

brightnessData.note: Molar brightness at −70 mV from Villette et al. 2019 Table 1 = 15 mM⁻¹cm⁻¹ = 15000 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ (absolute); EGFP reference 56000 × 0.60 = 33600 → 15000/33600 ≈ 0.446. Consistent with the independent 37.5 %EGFP direct measurement in Rühl et al. 2024. (Was 0.748, computed with the incorrect 20040 anchor and mis-sourced to Fig. S5D.)

Molar brightness at −70 mV, Villette et al. 2019 Table 1: ASAP3 = 15 mM⁻¹cm⁻¹ vs Ace2N-4aa-mNeon ≈ 90 mM⁻¹cm⁻¹ (values from Gong et al. 2015) → 15/90 ≈ 0.167. Completes the Table 1 brightness row, which was already harvested for ArcLight, Archon1 and QuasAr2/3 but not for Ace2N-mNeon. The Ace2N-mNeon value is given as an approximate (≈90) in the table; consistent with that page's independent 2.76×EGFP entry (0.446/2.76 = 0.162).

Relative brightness under one-photon widefield 470/24-nm illumination in HEK293-Kir2.1 cells, quantified as the GEVI/mCherry (green/red) fluorescence ratio; n = 4 independent transfections per GEVI. ASAP2s is the normalization reference (1.00); the ASAP3 mean line reads ≈0.87 (difference n.s.), JEDI-1P ≈2.35. Cross-GEVI entry from the JEDI-1P origin paper. Consistent with the 2P Fig. 2I value already stored on the ASAP2s page (ASAP2s/ASAP3 = 1.11 → 0.90) and with JEDI-2P Fig. S4I (≈0.89 under 1PM).

photostabilityData.note: ASAP3-Kv in primary cultured mouse neurons, n=11 cells, 475-nm LED continuous illumination at 25 mW/mm² (Piatkevich et al. 2019 Ext. Fig. 5e source data, MOESM12). Illumination corrected from a prior '1500 mW/mm²' value, which was the SomArchon red-laser intensity (637 nm) mis-copied onto this green/cpGFP sensor; the green channel in that figure is 25 mW/mm². F/F0 = 0.529 at 300 s (matches the digitized photobleach entry from the same panel).

~40% photobleaching over a 1-h recording of ASAP3 in PV interneurons in mouse cortex under CW 445-nm exposure (~10 µW/mm²), versus ~10% for ASAP7y under the same conditions (green ASAP3 trace ends at ~64% at 60 min in Ext. Data Fig. 3a). Cross-measured in the ASAP7y paper (Hao et al. 2026); ASAP3, but not ASAP7y, shows reversible photobleaching (sawtooth recovery at periodic 445-nm bouts).

apWidthData.sample: HEK293A cells, optical response to a single AP-like command waveform, whole-cell voltage clamp
apWidthData.note: Optical response width (FWHM) to a single AP-like command waveform (2-ms FWHM, +30 mV peak), HEK293A whole-cell voltage clamp, fluorescence acquired at ~987 Hz (ORCA Flash 4.0 V2 sCMOS; the paper's Methods repeatedly specify ~987 fps/Hz for green-GEVI voltage imaging, not a round 1 kHz). Fig. 2f y-axis is 'Width of response to spike waveforms (ms)' and the caption states 'The width corresponds to the full-width at half-maximum' (so this IS a true FWHM, not a 30%-max width). Re-measured 2026-09 by pixel calibration off the rendered panel: ASAP3 (orange) mean line ≈ 5.7-5.8 ms, ASAP2s ≈ 6.7-6.9 ms, JEDI-1P (primary subject) ≈ 4.85 ms; n = 8 ASAP3 cells. Independently corroborated by JEDI-2P Fig. S4F (same 2-ms AP-waveform protocol, ≈5.6 ms). Experiments done at room temperature (Fig. 2 caption: 'unless otherwise noted'; the 32–35 °C note applies only to panels m–o).

apWidthData.sample: Cultured rat hippocampal neurons, optical response to current-evoked single APs, current clamp, room temperature
apWidthData.note: Optical spike width at half-maximum (FWHM ≈ 12.7 ms, n = 5) of the ASAP3 optical single-AP waveform in cultured hippocampal neurons, read from the 'Optical spike width (ms)' bar chart in Fig. 2F of the origin paper (Villette et al. 2019); the co-plotted ASAP2s bar is ≈17.3 ms. Measured under one-photon widefield illumination at room temperature. samplingRate is omitted: the paper reports only a range (1–2 kHz, Table 1 footnote) rather than a single frame rate for this experiment, and this width (~12.7 ms) is dominated by ASAP3's own deactivation kinetics (τ_off ~16–32 ms at RT) rather than the frame interval (kinetics-dominated exception), so it is meaningful but not strictly comparable to frame-rate-specified widths. Distinct from the electrical AP FWHM (3.9 ± 0.2 ms) also reported in Fig. 2E, which is the command AP waveform, not the optical response.

Optical spike FWHM ≈ 3.4 ms (grey ASAP3 bar) read off the 'Spike FWHM (ms)' bar sub-panel of Fig. 3f in the 2Photron paper (Villette et al. 2024 bioRxiv), where ASAP3 (grey) is cross-plotted with JEDI-2P (green, ≈1.85 ms) and 2Photron-ST552 (red, ≈1.42 ms). ASAP3 data are from Villette et al. 2019 (n=23 cells) as noted in the caption. Two-photon ULoVE recording (3.75 kHz is the 2Photron paper's own ULoVE rate; the re-plotted ASAP3 data were acquired by Villette et al. at 3-5 kHz). No numeric ASAP3 value is given in the text; value verified by rendering and reading the bar height against the y-axis (0–4 ms). Cross-measured in the 2Photron paper.

apWidthData.sample: HEK293A cells, optical response to a single AP-like command waveform (2-ms FWHM, +30 mV peak), whole-cell voltage clamp
apWidthData.note: Full width at half maximum of the fluorescence response to a single AP waveform under widefield one-photon microscopy (JEDI-2P paper Fig. S4F, caption: 'Full width at half maximum of the fluorescence response to single action potential waveforms'); n = 7 ASAP3 HEK293A cells. Time series captured at 1 kHz on an ORCA Flash 4.0 V2 sCMOS at room temperature (Methods). Pixel-calibrated off the published panel: ASAP2s ≈ 6.9 ms, ASAP3 ≈ 5.6 ms, JEDI-2P ≈ 5.1 ms. Cross-GEVI entry from the JEDI-2P origin paper; agrees with the ≈5.8 ms measured by the same protocol in JEDI-1P Fig. 2f.

photobleach.note: Two-photon in-vivo photobleaching of ASAP3-Kv in mouse cortical L2/3 neurons of awake head-fixed mice, digitized from the green Pattern 3 (ULoVE) curve of Fig. 4D-left (log-log 'Normalized flux' vs 'Time (s)'; n = 17 cells). Ti:sapphire 920 nm, 80 MHz, 20 mW post-objective, 25x 0.95-NA objective; the 9-focus multiplexed-line ULoVE pattern is the configuration used for every in-vivo ASAP3-Kv recording in this paper. Digitized by colour-masking the green trace with a two-point log calibration (decade ticks at 10^-4...10^2 s on x, 1.0 and 0.1 on y) and overlay-verified against the panel. Model-free t75 = 2.5 s; the curve never falls to 50% in the 62-s window (it ends at F/F0 = 0.70), so no t50 is stored. The co-plotted grey Pattern 1 curve (a conventional diffraction-limited 2P spot, n = 24 cells) bleaches far faster on the same axes - model-free t75 = 5 ms and t50 = 0.39 s, ending at F/F0 = 0.14 at 62 s - which is the ~40x photobleaching reduction that motivates ULoVE; it is not stored as a separate entry because it is the same sensor under a control illumination geometry. The companion bar chart in Fig. 4D-right quantifies the same data as % photobleaching at 0.1, 1, 10, 60 and 300 s. 2P entry: intensityMWmm2 is deliberately OMITTED - a 2P point-scanning dose is not comparable to the 1P 100 mW/mm2 reference and must not be linearly dose-scaled. The fit is a power law (a=0.787, b=-0.0335, R2=0.968), the best of the viewer's supported models across the six decades of time spanned here; a biexponential reaches R2=0.974 but places its own 75% crossing at 0.8 s, three-fold off the model-free value, so the power law was preferred. The stored t75 is the model-free crossing, not the fit's.

Cross-GEVI photobleaching from the same Fig. S4 46 mW/mm² panel as JEDI-1P (measured alongside it; 470/24-nm widefield, HEK293T, n=11). The published trace is brightness relative to ASAP2s; the ASAP3 (orange) curve was re-normalized to its own first frame → F/F0. Half-life t50 ≈ 295 s, extrapolated well beyond the 120 s window (curve ends at F/F0≈0.70; relies on the slow component τ2≈562 s). Stored as t50 (not t75) to match the figure's other curves, whose 75% crossings fall in the shared rapid-initial-photobleach transient. NOTE: in fractional (F/F0) terms ASAP3 bleaches slightly LESS than the much brighter JEDI-1P here — JEDI-1P's advantage in this figure is its larger photon budget (absolute brightness), not lower fractional bleaching.

In-vivo 1P photostability digitized from Fig. 2b (ASAP3-Kv, green), hippocampal SST+ interneurons, continuous 453-nm widefield at 100 mW/mm², acquired in 11-s bouts time-binned to 500 fps. Noisy in-vivo trace; ends at F/F0≈0.77 at 75 s, so t75≈95 s is extrapolated just past the window. Measured alongside ASAP4b/ASAP4e (same figure → cross-overlay).

Cross-GEVI entry from the JEDI-2P origin paper (primary subject JEDI-2P): 1P photobleaching of ASAP3 in HEK293-Kir2.1 cells, widefield 1PM at 15 mW/mm² over 5 min (Fig. S4G, orange curve). Digitized by HSV color separation. Large fast-bleach initial drop (to ~0.64), so the t75% crossing is transient-dominated → half-life t50 ≈ 59 s stored instead. Biexponential fit. Companion curves in the same panel: JEDI-2P, ASAP2s.

Cross-GEVI photobleaching from the SomArchon paper (Piatkevich et al. 2019, primary subject SomArchon). ASAP3-Kv (cpGFP, KV2.1-targeted) in primary cultured mouse neurons (n=11), 475 nm LED at 25 mW/mm² continuous illumination, digitized from the exact Ext. Data Fig. 5e source data (MOESM12 spreadsheet). F/F0 falls to 0.529 at 300 s and never reaches 50% in-window, so the model-free t75 = 95 s is stored (no t50; the t75 crossing is in the sustained phase, not a rapid initial transient). Biexponential fit, R²=0.998. CAVEAT (cross-overlay): the Ext. Fig. 5e panel co-plots this green sensor with SomArchon, which was imaged at 637 nm / 1,500 mW/mm² — a ~60x higher intensity at a different wavelength. intensityMWmm2 is OMITTED (no dose-scaling) because the cross-sensor comparison is NOT apples-to-apples across that wavelength/intensity gap. NB: this page's separate photostabilityData Ext.-Fig.-5e entry currently lists '1500 mW/mm²' for ASAP3-Kv, which is the SomArchon red-laser value mis-copied; the green channel here is 25 mW/mm².

Cross-GEVI in-vivo photobleaching from the ASAP7y paper (Hao et al. 2026 bioRxiv, primary subject ASAP7y). ASAP3 (green) expressed in mouse cortical PV interneurons, co-plotted with ASAP7y (yellow) over a 1-h continuous recording under CW 445-nm exposure (~10 µW/mm²); the green ASAP3 curve was digitized by color-masking with the correct 0-min (x=349 px) → 60-min (x=1619 px) tick calibration. The net trend falls from 100% to ~64% at 60 min (~40% photobleaching vs ~10% for ASAP7y, per caption). NON-MONOTONIC SAWTOOTH: ASAP3 (but not ASAP7y) undergoes REVERSIBLE photobleaching — the curve drops then recovers at each periodic 445-nm bout, so the stored trace is the median-line envelope and reflects real reversible-recovery physiology, not a digitization artifact. No biexponential fit is stored (the sawtooth makes a monotonic-decay model inappropriate, R²<0). t75 = 886 s is the first (model-free) crossing below 0.75; because of the reversible recovery the signal transiently returns above 0.75 until ~20 min. t50 never reached in-window.
